Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Global Safety Officer, Medical Director, Obesity and related conditions


What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will serve as the strategic safety leader for assigned the Obesity and related conditions therapeutic area within Amgen's global development organization. You will be accountable for the overall benefit-risk profile, safety strategy, signal management, and safety governance of clinical programs.


This role is ideal for a physician who has served as a Global Safety Officer (GSO), Clinical Safety Lead, Safety Lead Physician, or equivalent accountable safety leader for development-stage assets and has directly influenced key clinical development decisions through safety leadership.

You will establish the strategy, direction, and priorities of pharmacovigilance activities and will be accountable for the overall safety profile and safety-related decisions for assigned products.


You will lead the Safety Analysis Team (SAT), Global Safety Team (GST), and serve as a core member of the Executive Safety Committee (ESC). You will partner closely with Clinical Development, Translational Medicine, Regulatory, Biostatistics, and Medical Affairs to influence development strategy and support innovative therapies for patients with rare diseases and high unmet medical need.


Responsibilities

  • Serve as the accountable physician safety leader for assigned Obesity development programs.
  • Lead global safety strategy for clinical development programs.
  • Partner with Clinical Development and Translational Medicine teams to inform dose-escalation, cohort expansion, proof-of-concept, and development decisions.
  • Provide medical safety leadership and contribute to benefit-risk evaluations throughout clinical development.
  • Review and interpret emerging safety data and communicate safety implications to development teams and governance committees.
  • Lead Safety Analysis Team (SAT), Global Safety Team (GST), and participate in Executive Safety Committee (ESC) discussions.
  • Review and contribute to Safety Review Committees (SRCs), Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs), and other safety governance forums.
  • Validate safety signals and lead signal detection, assessment, and risk evaluation activities.
  • Develop and maintain Core Safety Information including Core Data Sheets and informed consent safety language.
  • Prepare and review Risk Management Plans (RMPs), risk minimization strategies, and aggregate safety reports.
  • Lead safety review and provide strategic input into protocol development, CRF design, Statistical Analysis Plans, Clinical Study Reports, and safety monitoring plans.
  • Prepare and review safety sections of regulatory submissions including INDs, CTAs, BLAs, NDAs, and other global submissions.
  • Serve as the safety representative on Evidence Generation Teams and other cross-functional development teams.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Zayo provides mission-critical bandwidth to the world’s most impactful companies, fueling the innovations that are transforming our society. Zayo’s 141,000-mile network in North America and Europe includes extensive metro connectivity to thousands of buildings and data centers. Zayo’s communications infrastructure solutions include dark fiber, private data networks, wavelengths, Ethernet, and dedicated Internet access. Zayo serves wireless and wireline carriers, media, tech, content, finance, healthcare and other large enterprises.

Zayo Group is seeking an experienced Senior Software Engineer to join our Network Automation Software Engineering team. Our team develops and maintains the software platforms, microservices, and automation solutions that enable the provisioning, configuration, and management of Zayo's large-scale telecommunications network infrastructure.


In this role, you will design, develop, and maintain scalable, reliable software solutions that automate complex network operations and reduce the need for manual intervention. You will work primarily in Python, building distributed microservices that communicate through gRPC APIs defined using Protocol Buffers (Protobuf), and leverage Cisco Network Services Orchestrator (NSO) to automate network device configuration and service provisioning.


The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, understands distributed systems, and is interested in applying modern software engineering practices to network infrastructure. Experience with telecommunications or network automation is highly valued, but a solid software engineering foundation and the ability to learn new technologies are equally important.


Responsibilities

Software Development & Architecture

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain Python-based applications and microservices supporting network automation and orchestration.
  • Build and integrate gRPC-based services using Protocol Buffers to define strongly typed APIs and service contracts.
  • Design scalable, maintainable software architectures that support complex network provisioning and lifecycle management workflows.
  • Develop reusable software components, libraries, and APIs that integrate with internal systems and network infrastructure.
  • Write clean, efficient, well-documented, and thoroughly tested code following modern software engineering best practices.
  • Identify and resolve software defects, performance bottlenecks, and system reliability issues.
  • Participate in architectural discussions, technical design reviews, and technology decisions.

Network Automation & Orchestration

  • Develop automation solutions using Cisco NSO, including service models, service packages, and integrations with network devices.
  • Build software that interfaces with Cisco NSO APIs to automate network configuration, provisioning, and service lifecycle operations.
  • Collaborate with network engineering and operations teams to translate complex network requirements into reliable, repeatable automation workflows.
  • Develop automation that improves operational efficiency, reduces configuration errors, and accelerates service delivery.
  • Troubleshoot automation workflows involving multiple services, systems, and network devices.

DevOps & Infrastructure

  • Develop, maintain, and improve GitLab CI/CD pipelines to automate application testing, building, and deployment.
  • Package and deploy applications using Docker containers, with services hosted and orchestrated through Docker Swarm.
  • Support the operation, monitoring, troubleshooting, and ongoing reliability of production microservices.
  • Implement automated testing, code quality checks, and deployment processes to improve software delivery and reliability.
  • Promote DevOps principles and continuous improvement across the development lifecycle.

Collaboration & Technical Leadership

  • Work within an Agile development environment, participating in sprint planning, daily standups, backlog refinement, code reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Collaborate with software engineers, network engineers, product stakeholders, and operations teams to deliver high-quality automation capabilities.
  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers, providing technical guidance, code review feedback, and support for professional growth.
  • Take ownership of complex technical initiatives from initial design through implementation, deployment, and production support.
  • Advocate for engineering best practices, including automated testing, maintainable code, documentation, and thoughtful system design.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to simplify existing systems, reduce technical debt, and improve the performance and reliability of our automation platforms.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of professional software development experience, with demonstrated experience designing and delivering production software.
  • Strong proficiency in Python, including object-oriented programming, asynchronous programming, API development, and automated testing.
  • Experience building and maintaining microservices or distributed applications.
  • Hands-on experience with gRPC and Protocol Buffers, or significant experience with similar API development technologies and the ability to quickly learn gRPC.
  • Solid understanding of software design principles, data structures, algorithms, and common architectural patterns.
  • Experience with Git-based source control and collaborative development workflows, including merge requests and code reviews.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and automated software delivery processes.
  • Practical experience developing and deploying containerized applications using Docker.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex applications and diagnosing issues across multiple interacting services.
  • Strong communication skills, analytical problem-solving abilities, and the ability to collaborate effectively across technical disciplines.

Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with Cisco NSO, including service packages, YANG models, Python APIs, and network service orchestration.
  • Experience with GitLab CI/CD and Docker Swarm in production environments.
  • Familiarity with network automation technologies and protocols such as NETCONF, RESTCONF, SSH, and YANG.
  • Understanding of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, routing, switching, VLANs, MPLS, BGP, and common telecommunications network architectures.
  • Experience designing and integrating systems for network provisioning, configuration management, or service activation.
  • Experience with distributed systems concepts, including service-to-service communication, concurrency, fault tolerance, retries, and error handling.
  • Familiarity with observability practices, including structured logging, metrics, monitoring, and distributed tracing.
  • Experience working with relational or non-relational databases.
  • Knowledge of Linux systems, shell scripting, and application deployment practices.
  • Experience with automated testing frameworks such as pytest and integration testing strategies.
  • Prior experience in the telecommunications, service provider, or large-scale network infrastructure industries.

What Success Looks Like

  • Deliver production-ready software that improves the speed, accuracy, and reliability of network provisioning and configuration.
  • Take technical ownership of significant components of our automation ecosystem.
  • Contribute to the design and evolution of our Python microservices and gRPC-based architecture.
  • Help improve the stability, maintainability, and operational visibility of our production systems.
  • Partner effectively with network engineering teams to turn complex operational requirements into scalable software solutions.
  • Raise the technical bar of the team through code quality, mentorship, and continuous improvement.

Why Join Our Team?

At Zayo, network automation plays a critical role in enabling the scale, reliability, and operational efficiency of our telecommunications infrastructure.

Our engineering team works at the intersection of modern software development and large-scale network infrastructure, solving challenging problems that have a direct impact on how network services are delivered and managed.

1099 Clinical Opportunities

FUTURE OPPORTUNITIES ONLY: This is an interest form for potential future independent contractor opportunities at Parsley Health, not a currently available contract. There is no specific opening or hiring timeline associated with this posting.

Interested in working with Parsley Health? Let's connect.

Parsley Health is the leading functional healthcare company in the U.S., founded by Dr. Robin Berzin with a mission to transform how we treat chronic conditions through root-cause, whole-person medicine.

Our clinicians combine advanced diagnostics, personalized lifestyle interventions, and meaningful patient relationships to help members improve their health. We provide the clinical tools, resources, and collaborative support needed to deliver excellent care.

We're always interested in connecting with experienced MDs, DOs, NPs, and PAs who may be interested in providing care to Parsley members on a part-time, independent contractor basis.

Whether you have your own practice, work with other organizations, or are exploring additional clinical opportunities, we'd love to learn more about you.

Why reach out now?

One of the first things we do when we're looking for additional clinical coverage is review clinicians who have already expressed interest in working with Parsley.

Our needs are often very specific. We may need a clinician licensed in a particular state, available for a certain number of hours or on specific days, or someone with a particular area of clinical expertise or functional medicine training.

By sharing your licenses, experience, background, and ideal availability now, you're helping us understand where there might be a fit before we even have a specific opening.

By the time we publicly post an opportunity, we may already be speaking with clinicians whose qualifications and availability match what we need.

Whether you're actively looking for additional work, considering expanding your practice, or simply open to future opportunities, we'd encourage you to connect with us now.

What contracting with Parsley could look like

Depending on our future clinical needs, opportunities may include:

  • Part-time independent contractor arrangements with varying weekly commitments

  • Virtual patient care, with potential in-person opportunities depending on location and need

  • Collaboration with our clinical team, including health coaches and RN care managers

  • Access to Parsley's clinical technology platform and resources

  • The ability to maintain an independent practice or other professional commitments, subject to applicable disclosure, conflict-of-interest, confidentiality, and patient protection requirements

  • Parsley provides malpractice coverage for care delivered to our members. Independent contractors are responsible for maintaining their own required licenses and associated expenses.

Who we'd love to connect with

  • Licensed MDs, DOs, NPs, and PAs with active state licensure and applicable board certification

  • Clinicians with 3+ years of relevant clinical experience, ideally in primary care

  • Clinicians with professional experience practicing functional, integrative, or longevity medicine

  • Clinicians who have completed or are pursuing formal functional medicine training or certifications

  • People who value personalized patient care, clinical collaboration, and flexibility

  • Functional medicine experience and formal training are especially valuable to us, but we also welcome interest from clinicians who are earlier in their functional medicine journey.

Tell us what you're looking for

Our application asks about your clinical credentials, state licenses, functional medicine experience, formal training and certifications, ideal availability, hourly rate expectations, and what interests you about working with Parsley.

We'll also ask whether you're actively seeking additional clinical work or would consider an opportunity sometime in the future.

We'll review your information when relevant opportunities arise and reach out if there's a potential fit between your qualifications, interests, availability, and our clinical needs.

There is no need to wait for an active opportunity to introduce yourself!


Please note: This is an expression of interest in potential future independent contractor arrangements, not an application for a currently available contract. Submitting your information does not guarantee an interview, engagement, or a specific response timeline. Any future contractor arrangement is subject to applicable legal and clinical requirements.

Parsley Health is committed to equal opportunity and building an inclusive clinical team.


Important note: If you're selected to move forward in a future selection process, a member of our Talent Acquisition team will contact you from an @parsleyhealth.com email address. We will never conduct interviews through Microsoft Teams, request your banking information during recruitment, or send you a check to purchase equipment.

Who is USP?

The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide.

At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health.

USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment.

Brief Job Overview

This role is critical to advancing USP’s mission of protecting patient safety and improving global health by ensuring strong regional execution, trusted partnerships, and sustainable growth throughout Latin America.

The Regional Manager & Sr. Director, Latin America (LATAM) is responsible for strategic leadership, operational execution, and sustainable growth of USP’s mission, programs, and commercial activities across Latin America. This role serves as USP’s senior regional executive, accountable for strengthening USP’s public health impact, regulatory engagement, stakeholder relationships, and financial performance in a diverse and highly regulated environment.

The RM & Sr. Director LATAM will lead multidisciplinary teams across Scientific Programs, Strategic Customers Development, External Affairs, Marketing and Operations, while ensuring full alignment with USP’s global strategy, values, and quality standards.

USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards.

Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments.

jobs.excerpt: The short version You’ll be second in command of a client pod, sitting directly beside a senior Retention Strategist and learning to do their job while you’re still doing yours.
jobs.description:
The short version
You’ll be second in command of a client pod, sitting directly beside a senior Retention Strategist and learning to do their job while you’re still doing yours.
Most agency roles at this level hand you a brief and expect you to build it. This one expects you to read the brief, understand why it exists, and tell us when it’s wrong.

Why this role exists
We run client work in pods. Each pod has a Strategist who owns the thinking, the client relationship and the revenue outcome; an Activations Specialist who owns the technical build and QA in Klaviyo; plus a designer and a copywriter.
We kept hitting the same gap. The Strategist gets pulled into execution when things get busy. The Activations Specialist can execute anything but hasn’t been trained to think about why. Neither can fully cover the other.

So we’re building the seat in between.

You’re the Strategist’s right hand. When they’re on a client call, you’re moving the pod. When they’re on leave, you hold the account. When the Activations Specialist is buried, you build. You’re the person who knows enough about both sides to keep an account running without either one of them in the room.
That’s a lot of responsibility for a junior seat. It’s also the fastest way we know to make someone a strategist.

What you’ll learn here
This is the part most job posts skip, so we’ll be specific.
You’ll learn to diagnose instead of guess. Klaviyo revenue is down 20% this month. Is that a flow problem, a deliverability problem, a list fatigue problem, or is store revenue just down and email is fine? Most people at your level can’t tell those apart. You’ll learn to, on real accounts, with a senior strategist checking your reasoning.
You’ll learn what actually moves retention revenue. Flow architecture, segmentation, offer strategy, cadence. Not formatting tweaks, not sending more email.
You’ll learn to think in leverage. On any account there are twenty things you could do. Two of them matter. Picking those two is the entire job of a strategist, and it’s a skill you build by being asked the question every week until you have an answer.
You’ll learn to own a client narrative. What happened, why it happened, what we’re doing about it. Delivered clearly enough that a client trusts you in a bad month, not just a good one.
You’ll sit in gameplan reviews, standups and client calls with senior strategists from day one. You’ll be asked for your view. You’ll be wrong sometimes and told why.
Do this well and you’re running your own pod as a full Strategist inside 12 to 18 months. That’s not a vague promise. It’s the path, and we’ve moved people down it.

What you’ll actually do
Execute at a level that never needs checking. Build flows, campaigns, segments and popups in Klaviyo. Triggers, filters, conditional splits, send windows, suppression logic, UTMs. Correct the first time.
Own QA like your name is on it. Rendering across Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook. Live links. Dynamic content resolving properly. Exclusions actually excluding. A send with an error is worse than a late send, and you’re the last line before it goes out.
Question the brief. This is the part we mean seriously. If a flow doesn’t make sense, if a segment will overlap with something already live, if the timing will cannibalise a campaign — say it before you build, not after. Executing a bad brief perfectly is still a bad outcome, and we’d rather you push back.
Read the numbers and form a view. Pull the data, then tell us what it means. “Browse abandonment RPR dropped 30% after we changed the segment” is worth more than a clean export.
Keep production honest. ClickUp current in real time. Blockers flagged the moment you see them, not the day of the deadline. Nobody should have to chase you.
Step into either seat when the pod needs it. Cover the Strategist on a call or a weekly update. Cover the build when the Activations Specialist is stretched.

Who this is for
You’re already fast in the tools. This part isn’t negotiable.

  • 2+ years hands-on in Klaviyo for an ecommerce brand or agency. Not “familiar with.” You’ve built multi-branch flows, written nested segment logic, debugged a trigger that wasn’t firing, and know exactly where Klaviyo’s date-relative filters trip people up.
  • Working knowledge of Shopify — how the integration feeds Klaviyo, what the standard events and properties are, where the data breaks.
  • Comfortable with the wider stack (reviews, subscriptions, loyalty, SMS, popups) and able to figure out a new tool without a walkthrough.
  • You want to know why, and you ask.
  • You flag what looks wrong even when it isn’t strictly yours.
  • You can explain a decision in one sentence.
  • You manage your own timelines.

You think past the ticket.

You don’t need to be the smartest person in the room. You need to be curious, accurate, and hard to rattle. We’ll teach you the rest.
This isn’t for you if: you want a pure strategy seat and expect someone else to build. In this role you build, and the building is what earns you the strategic seat.

Setup
Fully remote, full-time. A defined portfolio of ecommerce clients, a small pod you’ll work with daily, and direct access to senior strategists and managers. You will not be left to figure it out alone.

jobs.description:
Why Valtech? We’retheexperience innovation company - a trusted partner to the world’s most recognized brands. To our people we offer growth opportunities, a values-driven culture, international careers and the chance to shape the future of experience.

The opportunity

At Valtech, you’ll find an environment designed for continuous learning, meaningful impact, and professional growth. Whether you're pioneering new digital solutions, challenging conventional thinking or building the next generation of customer experiences, your work will help transform industries.

We are proud of:

  • The work we do and the innovation we drive
  • Our values of share, care and dare
  • A workplace culture that fosters creativity, diversity and autonomy
  • Our borderless, global framework, which enables seamless collaboration

The role

We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Senior Developer to support the migration of an enterprise digital platform from Sitecore to Contentful.

The role involves both content migration and the migration of existing applications, React/Typescript development, API integrations and modern headless architectures.

We are also looking for someone with an AI-first mindset who embraces AI-assisted and spec-driven development to improve delivery speed, quality and consistency, while retaining ownership of technical judgement and code quality.

Key Responsibilities

Application and Content Migration

  • Migrate and modernise existing Sitecore-backed applications to work with Contentful.
  • Develop, refactor and enhance frontend applications using React and TypeScript.
  • Replace Sitecore-specific dependencies, components and integrations with Contentful-compatible solutions.
  • Develop content migration tooling, scripts and automated transformation processes.
  • Implement Contentful content models, API integrations and content delivery patterns.
  • Ensure migrated applications maintain functionality, performance, accessibility and quality.

AI-Native Engineering

  • Adopt an AI-first mindset, proactively identifying opportunities to accelerate development, migration and problem-solving using AI.
  • Apply spec-driven development, using clear technical specifications, acceptance criteria and tests to guide AI-assisted implementation.
  • Leverage AI to support Sitecore analysis, schema mapping, migration script generation, application refactoring and validation.
  • Use AI coding assistants effectively while reviewing, testing and taking accountability for generated outputs.
  • Share AI-enabled development practices and contribute to improving team productivity.

Engineering Quality and Collaboration

  • Independently own complex development tasks and significant migration components.
  • Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and contribute to CI/CD and automated testing.
  • Identify technical risks, dependencies and opportunities for improvement.
  • Collaborate with Lead Developers, architects, QA and content teams.
  • Support less experienced developers through mentoring, code reviews and knowledge sharing.

Essential Skills and Experience

  • Strong commercial software engineering experience, particularly with React and TypeScript.
  • Experience migrating, modernising or refactoring existing frontend applications.
  • Practical experience with headless CMS platforms, preferably Contentful, and an understanding of Sitecore.
  • Strong understanding of APIs, integration patterns and content modelling.
  • Experience with backend development, migration scripting or data transformation.
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools and an understanding of spec-driven development approaches.
  • Experience with automated testing, CI/CD and modern engineering practices.
  • Ability to work independently, solve complex problems and influence technical implementation decisions.

Desirable Experience

  • Direct experience migrating Sitecore applications and content to Contentful.
  • Experience with Next.js, Sitecore JSS or CMS/DXP replatforming.
  • Experience applying AI to content analysis, migration automation, code transformation or test generation.
  • Experience with multilingual, multisite or composable digital platforms.

If you do not meet all the listed qualifications or have gaps in your experience, we still encourage you to apply. At Valtech, we recognize that talent comes in many forms, and we value diverse perspectives and a willingness to learn.

Commitment to reaching all kinds of people

We design experiences that work for all kinds of people - and that starts with our own teams. At Valtech, we’re intentional about building an inclusive culture where everyone feels supported to grow, thrive and achieve their goals. No matter your background, you belong here. Explore our Diversity & Inclusion site to see how we’re creating a more equitable Valtech for all.

The benefits

This is a position based in Poland.

Mental and physical health:

  • 24 working days of paid vacation
  • National holidays covered
  • Sick leave (up to 20/year)
  • Unpaid leave (up to 20/year)
  • Medical insurance
  • Multisport card OR Multikafeteria
  • Maternity & paternity leave support

Personal and professional development:

  • Internal workshops & learning initiatives
  • Professional certifications reimbursement
  • Participation in professional local & global communities
  • Growth Framework to manage expectations and define the steps to move towards the selected career
  • Mentoring program with the ability to become a mentor or a mentee to grow to a higher position

Valtech Poland has a system of progressive benefit packages – the longer you stay with the company, the more benefits you get!

Beyond a competitive compensation package, we offer:

  • Flexibility, with remote and hybrid work options (country-dependent)
  • Career advancement, with international mobility and professional development programs
  • Learning and development, with access to cutting-edge tools, training and industry experts

Your application process

Once you apply, our Talent Acquisition team will review your application. Your CV should cover key information on relevant experiences and expertise. We do not require information such as age, gender, marital status, or a headshot in your application. We review all candidates based on skills, experience, and potential.

⚠️ Beware of recruitment fraud!

We are committed to inclusion and accessibility. If you need reasonable accommodations during the interview process, please either indicate it in your application or let your Talent Partner know.

About Valtech

Valtech is the experience innovation company that exists to unlock a better way to experience the world. By blending crafts, categories, and cultures, we help brands unlock new value in an increasingly digital world.

At the intersection of data, AI, creativity, and technology, we drive transformation for leading organizations, including L’Oréal, Mars, Audi, P&G, Volkswagen Dolby, and more.

At Valtech, we don’t just talk about transformation. We make it happen. Our people are the heart of our success, and we foster a workplace where everyone has the support to thrive, grow and innovate.

Are you ready to create what’s next? Join us.

jobs.title: Heartland Fund Rural Democracy Policy & Program Senior Manager
jobs.excerpt: Heartland Fund, part of the Rural Democracy Initiative (RDI), is seeking a Rural Democracy Policy and Program Senior Manager.
jobs.description:
Heartland Fund, part of the Rural Democracy Initiative (RDI), is seeking a Rural Democracy Policy and Program Senior Manager. This position requires a strategic thinker who is committed to building a thriving democracy and rural communities. They will develop and manage a portfolio of grantees, convene rural policy partners and drive key rural policy outcomes, and inform our strategy.

We are looking for a collaborative team player with experience building powerful civic, political, and/or policy infrastructure that advances community solutions, ideally for rural people and places. The successful candidate will be service-oriented, an excellent writer, able to manage competing priorities and deadlines, and balance many strategic considerations.

You will have an opportunity to help us enable equitable investment in rural communities, democracy, and climate solutions. This is a unique and dynamic position with opportunities for growth and impact as the Heartland Fund prepares to launch as an independent entity in 2027.

This is a remote position with a salary range of $85,000 to $100,000 and includes a generous benefits package.

About the Organization

As a funder collaborative, the Heartland Fund scales investment, supports local leaders, and builds long-term partnerships with rural and Native organizations to create thriving places where rural working people can determine our own futures, strengthening the entire nation. Heartland's grantmaking and programmatic investments support rural people working to transform their lives and communities toward shared prosperity, a healthy climate, and stronger democracy. We invest in building local capacity for issue advocacy, community organizing, economic development and local jobs, climate solutions, civic engagement, and sustainable urban-rural coalitions. We prioritize racial justice in all aspects of our work. In addition to grantmaking, Heartland also supports rural leaders and organizations through convening, research, and communications and storytelling.

Heartland Fund has three programs:

  • Rural Democracy builds civic power by investing in rural organizing infrastructure and leadership to ensure rural people have a meaningful say in the decisions that shape their lives.

  • Resource Rural (RR) mobilizes resources enabling rural communities to unlock public and private investment to create positive economic change in their communities.

  • Rural Climate Partnership (RCP) supports hometowns across America to accelerate climate solutions and build healthy local economies.

This position is with Heartland Fund’s 501(c)(3) Rural Democracy program that, alongside the 501(c)(4) Rural Victory Fund, comprises the Rural Democracy Initiative. RDI invests in civic engagement infrastructure in small towns and rural areas. Building power in these communities is essential to establishing an enduring pro-democracy, multiracial majority, and implementing the policies required for rural and small city communities to have vibrant, thriving futures.

Our coalition of rural innovators and aligned funders is working in more than 25 states across diverse regions. We support rural people working to transform rural America – and therefore the entire country – for decades to come.

Why Rural Democracy

Small town, small city and rural voters maintain disproportionate power to shape national policy and politics. Historically, a strong coalition of rural farmers and urban laborers advanced progress in this country, but in recent decades the leadership and funding infrastructure for progress has largely withdrawn from non-metro areas. At the same time, anti-democratic interests have invested heavily in rural voters. They’ve built organizing, policy, and communications machines to spread disinformation and ignite fears among rural electorates, promoting their own agendas to deepen divides.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities

The Policy and Program Senior Manager will support and help drive Rural Democracy’s grantmaking and policy strategy. They will be supervised by the Rural Democracy Senior Program Officer. The Policy and Program Senior Manager will manage a specific portfolio of grantees, where they will be responsible for cultivating trusting relationships, providing flexible resources, and assessing overall capacity needs. They will recommend timely investments that result in greater power and meaningful policy change for rural communities. They will also work closely with the Communications and Policy Director to co-lead and manage our bi-annual Rural Policy Action Summit and Rural Policy Action Report. Finally, they will build the capacity of our grantee network, communicate learning and success stories, and coordinate with key funding partners. The person holding this position will also work with the team on Rural Democracy’s affiliated project, Rural Victory Fund (RVF), to advance 501(c)(4) investments.

The Rural Democracy team takes pride in building an organizational culture rooted in learning, collaboration, racial justice, and a deep commitment to our mission. All staff are expected to provide leadership and vision to advance our mission, vision, and core strategies.

Grantmaking & Program Management

  • Develop and implement grantmaking strategies for assigned priority states.

  • Manage a policy and communications-focused grantmaking portfolio in addition to state-based grantmaking.

  • Conduct research and facilitate outreach in specific geographies, communities, and issue areas to advance our strategy.

  • Lead outreach to existing and new grantees and partners, including check-ins, collecting reports, and participating in site visits.

  • Gather, review and organize grant proposals, reports, and accompanying materials.

  • Prioritize and recommend grants. Support grant docket preparation.

  • Assess impacts and opportunities in partnership with field and funding partners.

Rural Policy Development

  • Co-lead and manage the bi-annual Rural Policy Action Summit by working with grantee and partner networks to organize a 50-person convening to shape federal policy and learn from each other.

  • Project manage and contribute to the bi-annual Rural Policy Action Report, which outlines federal policies, legislation, and executive action to strengthen rural communities.

  • Serve as a thought partner to democracy staff team members around policy best practices.

  • Support the grantee network in advancing rural policy priorities through resources, coaching, and peer-to-peer learning.

  • Help amplify policy efforts by contributing to policy-focused communications.

Program Support & Management

  • Support the Senior Program Officer and Strategic Partnerships team to meet requests from funders, stakeholders, partners, and aligned organizations.

  • Participate in grantee data collection processes including our bi-annual civic engagement survey, capacity building surveys, and political landscape summary.

  • Monitor and update grantmaking data systems in partnership with the Grants Management team.

  • Advance program priorities through Program Team meetings, retreats, grantee surveys, and work and project plans.

  • Facilitate grantee access to resources, tools, and capacity building opportunities.

Communications

  • Help the team showcase grantee success stories and lessons learned by identifying persuasive case examples and timely news for email newsletters, annual reports, and policy memos.

  • Translate impact stories, photos, quotes, and anecdotes from grantees into compelling content that supports fundraising efforts, including grant proposals and reports for our funders and donors.

Qualifications

We realize that great candidates may not have everything on this list. If you believe you would be a great fit for this role, we encourage you to apply.

Heartland Fund is seeking a strategic and ambitious team member who is excited to work in an entrepreneurial, fast paced, and creative environment. The person should exhibit a high degree of professionalism, initiative, and independence while also being collaborative and team focused. Specifically, the successful candidate will demonstrate:

Essential Skills & Characteristics

  • 7+ years of related work experience in a nonprofit, advocacy, government, intermediary, or foundation setting, and/or equivalent, working on projects with varied deadlines and deliverables.

  • Understanding of social change, civic engagement, public policy, or political strategy.

  • Significant experience with advancing policy change and navigating policy tradeoffs within coalitions, including connecting local and state priorities to federal policy.

  • Demonstrated commitment to racial justice and fluency with equity and anti-racist practices.

  • Demonstrated ability to listen deeply, hold space for different perspectives, and work with people from a variety of political, cultural, and social backgrounds

  • Strong writing and verbal communication skills, with an ability to clearly communicate an organization’s mission and impact.

  • Excellent relationship management skills with diverse constituencies, and a service orientation in grantee relationships.

  • Ability to work independently and drive complex projects involving a high degree of cross-organizational and external collaboration.

  • Demonstrated experience building and using organizational systems to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and complex projects, with exceptional attention to detail.

  • Acumen with event and convening organizing and facilitation, and working with coalitions.

  • Entrepreneurial and resourceful, a proactive and creative problem-solver.

  • Connection to and passion for rural people and places.

Preferred Skills & Knowledge

  • Experience in the philanthropic sector and with grantmaking.

  • Experience working on rural federal policy and/or with national advocacy organizations.

  • Understanding of the media and communications landscape, and the relationship between media and policy outcomes

  • An understanding of rural and small town America derived from either lived, professional, and/or volunteer experience.

  • Familiarity with a broad range of digital platforms and tools including Monday.com, Google Suite, Airtable, Fluxx, and Slack.

  • 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) nonprofit program management experience.

Compensation & Job Design

This is a full-time, exempt position. The organization is virtual, and the position will work remotely from their home within the United States. Occasional travel within the US. Expected compensation will be based on skills and relevant experience, with a starting salary range of $85,000 to $100,000.

The comprehensive benefits package includes 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance for employees (and their families). Employees are able to enroll in a 401k retirement plan and are eligible for a 3% automatic contribution and up to a 3% employer match on 401k contributions. Employees are also eligible for pre-tax transportation benefits. Employees will receive 120 hours of vacation time, 80 hours of health leave, up to 2 days of casual leave, and 20 hours of volunteer leave annually. Employees will also receive 13 paid holidays throughout the calendar year. Employees are eligible for 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave after 90 days of employment. All employees of Windward are required to complete timesheets.

Heartland Fund is a project of Windward Fund, a 501(c)(3) public charity that incubates new and innovative public-interest projects and grantmaking programs. Windward Fund is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining exceptional people and to creating a work environment that is dynamic, rewarding and enables each of us to realize our potential. Windward Fund’s work environment is safe and open to all employees and partners, respecting the full spectrum of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, political affiliation, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and all other classifications protected by law in the locality and/or state in which you are working.

The individual holding this position will also work part-time for an affiliated project, Rural Victory Fund, in Sixteen Thirty Fund, a 501(c)(4) organization, under a resource-sharing agreement between Windward Fund and Sixteen Thirty Fund. The responsibilities under that position will be overseen by Sixteen Thirty Fund.

Windward participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with employees’ Form I-9 information to confirm authorization to work in the United States. Job candidates and employees authorized to work may not be discriminated against on the basis of national origin or citizenship status.

How to Apply

Applications will be reviewed and considered on a rolling basis. A limited number of screening calls and interview spots will be filled starting in November 2026. Early applications are strongly encouraged. Desired start date in February 2027. Apply by submitting a cover letter and résumé to:

In your cover letter we are interested in learning why you are interested in this specific role at this time in your career, more about your connection to rural people and places, and the unique skills and talents you bring to this position. Anticipating a highly competitive applicant pool, candidates who demonstrate persuasive communications skills and rural policy experience will stand out in the process.

The Heartland Fund is partnering with Clover Search Works on this search. Questions regarding this opportunity are welcomed and can be directed to Julie Edsforth, julie(at)cloversearchworks.com.

Leidos is seeking an experienced Senior Network Support Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

In this role, you'll provide hands-on network operations, troubleshooting, and engineering support across a complex, geographically dispersed environment.   • DoD IAT Level II certification (Security+ or equivalent) required before starting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience using GitLab, CI/CD pipelines, Jira, and Confluence.

At Leidos, you'll have the opportunity to work with advanced networking technologies while supporting a mission that directly impacts the U.S. Army's global operations.

You'll collaborate with experienced network engineers, solve complex technical challenges, and help keep critical military communications secure and operational.

If you're an experienced Network Engineer with Cisco SD-WAN expertise who enjoys solving complex network challenges, we want to hear from you!

Join Leidos and help keep the Army connected. Apply today!

jobs.title: Bookkeeper & AR Specialist | Marketing Agency | Remote (LATAM) 📊
jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewOur client is a newsletter growth agency.
locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Our client is a newsletter growth agency. It runs paid Meta ads for newsletter and media brands, large personal brands and founders, and turns readers into revenue. Fees partly move with ad spend and contract terms. The founder launched it in early 2024, and it has grown from 0 to 30+ people in two years. The founder writes tactical posts and hosts a podcast. The team works remotely, and you'd talk with the founder and your manager on calls and in the finance channel on Slack.

Your Role

You're the person who gets the company paid. You own client invoicing, collections and the books in QuickBooks Online, working fully remote on US Eastern hours as a full-time contractor, reporting to the Operations Manager. The company went from 0 to 30+ people in two years, few finance steps are written down, and no senior finance person checks the work every day. So you run the whole loop and write the procedures as they settle. You start with the daily Mercury and Stripe check and the 4-week invoice cycle. The hardest balance is speed against accuracy: invoices go out on time, and the variable fees in them are calculated and checked before a client sees them. Get that right and cash arrives on schedule, the books close clean for the accountant or CPA, and the founder can trust the numbers.

What You'll Own

  • Run Stripe invoicing every 4 weeks, in advance, so each client gets a correct bill on time.

  • Work out variable fees from the contract and the ad spend report so every amount is right before it goes out.

  • Chase late payments every 3 working days and escalate quiet clients so cash comes in sooner.

  • Apply each incoming payment to the right invoice and keep the AR aging report current so the team sees who owes what.

  • Keep the QuickBooks Online books, reconcile bank, credit card, AR and AP, and run the monthly close so the outside accountant or CPA reviews clean numbers.

  • Set up new clients in Stripe, prepare final bills for leavers and support DocuSign contract admin so billing starts and ends cleanly.

  • Write down finance steps and maintain the trackers so the team can rely on them and the next hire can follow them.

A Week in the Role

  • You open Mercury and Stripe early and spot a failed charge and a renewal coming up. You post both in the start of day update on Slack, so the team knows what needs chasing.

  • A client is 3 working days past your last reminder. You send the next one from the shared AR mailbox, in the same thread, and add a dated note to the billing sheet. If the client goes quiet, you escalate.

  • A client on a variable fee comes due. You read the contract, pull the ad spend report, work out the fee and check it before sending. The invoice goes out right the first time.

  • A payment arrives that doesn't match its invoice. You trace it through the invoice, the payment and the bank line, then post what you found in the finance channel.

  • A new client signs. You create the payment link and subscription in Stripe and write down their billing terms, so the first invoice and every one after it use the same facts.

  • At month end you reconcile the bank and credit card accounts, close the books and hand them to the accountant or CPA. You write down any step you had to figure out along the way.

You Bring

  • A bachelor's degree in accounting or a related field, and three or 3 years in bookkeeping, billing or accounts receivable, including billing or collecting for dozens of active clients.

  • Experience running the full billing-to-cash cycle for recurring clients: sending invoices, tracking them on an AR aging report, chasing late payers, applying payments and reconciling.

  • Invoices you calculated from ad spend, usage or contract terms.

  • Working knowledge of QuickBooks Online (bank and credit card reconciliation, chart of accounts, AR and AP) and Excel, including a billing tracker you built or maintained.

  • A billing sheet, tracker or aging report that other people used, kept current with a date and the action taken on each entry.

  • Collections on a schedule with a set point for escalating, and a mismatch between an invoice, a payment and a bank line that you traced to its source.

  • Clear written and spoken English for client emails, daily updates and calls with the founder and your manager.

Bonus Points

  • Stripe for subscriptions, payment links and failed charges.

  • Mercury or another online business bank.

  • Invoicing in USD or work with US clients.

  • Multi-currency bank reconciliation.

What's Offered

  • What we'd estimate for a role like this: 1,000 to 1,500 USD a month, based on experience.

  • Fully remote from Latin America, on US Eastern hours.

  • Paid time off

Interview Process

1. First call: 30 minutes with us at atomic HR on what you have built, working terms and what you want next.
2. First interview: a conversation with the Operations Manager, who would be your manager, on how you have run invoicing, collections and month-end, and how the day-to-day of the seat would go.
3. Short practical test: a task drawn from the seat's own work, done on your own time. It checks that the amounts come out right and that you show how you got to them. We confirm the format and rough time before you start.
4. Call with the founder: a conversation on how you would work together on cash collection and the numbers, and on any questions you have about the company.

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Crossfoot, an AI-native accounting agent platform. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Crossfoot is agentic accounting for small-to-mid CPA firms; a segment where accountant shortages are structural, client intake is capped by production headcount, and the manual close and tax prep workflow consumes the majority of senior staff capacity. Crossfoot connects to the tools firms already use (QuickBooks Online, Xero, Drake) and delivers finished work products ready for partner review, without requiring system migration or enterprise-scale implementation.

Market Context

  • We didn't just build a thesis; we validated it directly with the market. We've spoken with CPA firm managing partners, CAS leads, and tax preparers. The key insights:

  • The "why now" is structural, not hype: the profession lost 300,000+ professionals from 2020–2024, and the replacement pipeline has shrunk ~33% in a decade. Firms now cap new-client intake by production headcount rather than demand. They turn away winnable work they can't staff. Meanwhile, CAS (advisory) revenue is projected to reach 30% of the firm's revenue by 2026.

  • Senior accountants spend 40%+ of their time on document intake and workbook compilation — $90K staff doing $20/hour data entry — while month-end close runs 10–15 business days on a pure manual process.

ROLE OVERVIEW

PulseLearning is looking for experienced facilitators to deliver and maintain customer training for one of our global software Clients.

You will be a strong expert in at least one of two product areas. The first is PIPE-FLO, used for fluid piping system modelling. The second is AGi32 and ElumTools, used for lighting design and analysis.

You will facilitate live training for engineering and design professionals, both virtually and in person, and manage the full learning event, from virtual classroom setup through to evaluation and reporting.

You will keep course content accurate and current, and use AI-enabled tools to work smarter and help shape how the training evolves. We are looking for someone who genuinely embraces AI and new ways of working, and who is excited to help keep this training modern, efficient, and engaging.

This is not a project based role and load will vary.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Facilitation and Delivery
    Facilitate scheduled live courses, both virtually and in person, typically one to two events per course each quarter.
  • Facilitate courses in one or both of these areas. PIPE-FLO: a 12-course series covering essential modelling skills, basic, pump, heat transfer, and control and instrument devices, custom pipes and fittings, data import and export, viscous and non-Newtonian fluids, closed loop systems, compressible gas analysis, and common modelling mistakes. AGi32 and ElumTools: introductory training (standard and relaxed pace), intermediate roadway lighting, basic interior and exterior lighting in ElumTools, and Revit with ElumTools for lighting designers.
  • Create an engaging, interactive learning environment that encourages questions, hands-on practice, and peer learning, whether online or in the room.
  • Adapt your facilitation style and pace to learners with different experience levels and needs.
  • Content Development and Maintenance
    Maintain and update course materials, exercises, and practice models so they stay current with new software releases.
  • Maintain version control so facilitators and learners always have the current materials.
  • Collaborate with Client subject matter experts and product teams to translate complex engineering concepts into clear, practical learning experiences.
  • Apply adult learning principles to course design and delivery, in line with the Client's learning objectives.
  • Develop or update facilitator guides, job aids, FAQs, and process documentation using approved source materials.
  • Virtual Classroom and Learning Event Administration
    Create and administer virtual classroom sessions using approved enterprise platforms.
  • Configure facilitator and producer access, participant settings, invitations, engagement features, and supporting learning materials, including virtual lab environments where used.
  • Partner with fellow facilitators to confirm session readiness, and support rehearsals where required.
  • Run polls, quizzes, knowledge checks, attendance tracking, and participant engagement activities.
  • Extract and reconcile attendance and interaction data, and prepare completion information for downstream processing when automated integration is unavailable.
  • Troubleshoot virtual learning issues and coordinate escalation to technical support where necessary.

Evaluation and Reporting

  • Create and validate survey and evaluation links based on the intended audience, learning modality (virtual or in person), and measurement requirements.
  • Run recurring and ad hoc reports across learning, media, survey, content, and collaboration platforms.
  • Review data for completeness and accuracy, investigate discrepancies, and clearly document any limitations.
  • Consolidate information from multiple sources using approved and repeatable processes.
  • Prepare clear reporting outputs and summaries for PulseLearning and Client stakeholders.
  • Maintain reporting schedules, templates, and instructions to support consistency and self-service.

Quality and Governance

  • Apply established requirements for naming conventions, version control, accessibility, privacy, and security across course materials and learner data.
  • Escalate quality, privacy, accessibility, or operational risks appropriately.
  • Identify recurring issues and suggest improvements to processes, guidance, and the learner experience.
  • Continuous Improvement and AI Enablement
    Embrace and champion AI and new ways of working, staying current with emerging tools and practices, and maintaining a willingness to adapt how courses are designed, delivered, and supported.
  • Use Microsoft 365 Copilot and approved AI or automation tools to improve efficiency and consistency, while remaining accountable for accuracy, confidentiality, quality, and final decisions.
  • Use AI-assisted tools, where appropriate, to support session preparation, content updates, exercise creation, learner feedback summaries, meeting notes, status updates, document reviews, and reporting.
  • Use approved AI tools to help identify missing, outdated, or inconsistent information in course materials and data, and to organise and reconcile attendance and evaluation data, with appropriate human review.
  • Ensure all AI-assisted outputs are reviewed and validated for technical accuracy before use with learners or the Client.
  • Act on learner feedback and evaluation results to improve both your facilitation and the course content.
  • Explore and recommend new delivery approaches, such as blended formats, shorter modules, and on-demand support for live sessions.
  • Identify repetitive tasks that may benefit from AI or automation, and contribute to testing and documenting safe, repeatable improvements.

Ways of Working

  • Take initiative, anticipate needs, and raise constraints and risks early.
  • Support knowledge transfer and onboarding of other facilitators where needed.
  • Work effectively with remote and globally distributed teams across multiple time zones.
  • Stay current with product updates, industry practice, facilitation and instructional design trends, and emerging learning technologies.

QUALIFICATIONS

Expert, hands-on knowledge of PIPE-FLO, AGi32, or ElumTools, gained through professional engineering, design, or applications work. Expertise in one product area is required. More than one is an advantage.

  • For PIPE-FLO: a background in fluid systems, piping, pumps, HVAC, or process engineering.
  • For AGi32 and ElumTools: a background in lighting design, lighting applications, or roadway lighting.
  • 3+ years of experience facilitating technical training for adult learners, with proven delivery in both virtual and in-person settings.
  • Confident, engaging presence, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and handle questions on the spot.
  • Hands-on experience setting up and running sessions on enterprise virtual classroom platforms such as Microsoft Teams, Zoom, or Webex, including engagement tools and attendance tracking.
  • Experience designing, developing, or updating technical courses and exercises.
  • Experience creating learner surveys and evaluations and producing reports from learning or survey platforms, with strong attention to data accuracy.
  • Practical experience using Microsoft 365 Copilot or other AI-enabled tools in content development, training delivery, or reporting, with a responsible approach to accuracy and confidentiality.
  • A genuine growth mindset and enthusiasm for AI and new ways of working, with a track record of adopting new tools and delivery methods and welcoming feedback on your facilitation.
  • Strong organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage course delivery, administration, and reporting alongside each other.
  • Strong learning agility and the ability to pick up new platforms and tools quickly.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Lighting, Education, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • A facilitation or train the trainer certification is an advantage, as is FLO-Master certification, Lighting Certified (LC), PE, or membership of the IES or Hydraulic Institute.
  • Experience with learning management systems, virtual lab environments, Autodesk Revit (for ElumTools), or eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline and Rise is desirable.
  • Must be able to pass and maintain a security clearance

Travel: Occasional travel for in-person delivery

About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the role

The AV BI Adjuster investigates, evaluates, and resolves bodily injury claims from incidents involving autonomous and driver-assist vehicles, including passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and occupants of other vehicles. The role combines traditional BI evaluation with analysis of who was in control, what the system did, and whether the claim should be resolved or defended.

What you'll do

  • Investigate and evaluate BI claims, building liability analysis on vehicle data, video, and remote-assistance records rather than statements alone
  • Contact claimants, witnesses, medical providers, and counsel promptly, documenting injuries, treatment, and damages
  • Set and maintain reserves that reflect liability, damages, venue, and representation
  • Negotiate and settle claims within authority, and recommend and document settlement strategy above it
  • Identify claims with litigation, product-liability, or regulatory risk and escalate early to the Litigation Adjuster and Team Lead, partnering with the AV operator’s safety and legal teams on sensitive or high-visibility incidents
  • Manage medical bills, liens, Medicare/Medicaid reporting, and settlement documentation, and maintain complete, audit-ready file notes explaining the liability and valuation decision

Who you are

  • Motivated and growth-oriented, excited by the prospect of building a tech-driven claims org
  • Passionate adjuster who cares about the customer experience and brings empathy and patience to everyone you interact with
  • Sense of urgency at all times (without working at all hours), paired with curiosity to learn the whole story so you can make the right decisions early and reach a prompt resolution
  • Creative problem-solver who finds the right exit ramp for resolving each claim in the insured’s best interest, and who isn’t afraid of conflict as long as it stays conversational rather than adversarial
  • Anti-status quo, acting on ideas for doing things differently, with strong communication skills and a collaborative, team-player attitude
  • Sense of humor, because claims are hard enough as it is, plus a detailed understanding of the SAE J3016 levels of driving automation (Levels 0–5), including how driver-assist (Levels 0–2) and driverless (Levels 3–5) systems shift responsibility among the human, the system, and the operator

Qualifications

  • 4–6+ years of bodily injury claims experience, preferably commercial auto, rideshare, or trucking
  • Strong medical-records review and injury valuation skills
  • Experience with represented claimants and attorney negotiation
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent claims experience
  • Proficiency in the claims system, document management, and Microsoft Office
  • Clear written and verbal communication with claimants, counsel, carriers, and client partners
  • Active adjuster license: resident-state license where available, otherwise a Designated Home State (DHS) license. Willing to obtain any additional required licenses within 60 days, including state testing.

Benefits

  • Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized!
  • Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work
  • 100% remote (home-based) role designed to support your work-life balance

Additionally, we will

  • Listen to your feedback to enhance and improve upon the long-standing challenges of an adjuster and the claims role
  • Work toward reducing and eliminating all the administrative work from an adjuster role
  • Foster a culture of empathy, transparency, and empowerment in a remote-first environment

At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you!

Job Description: Law Review Cite-Checker

Role Type: Contractor
Location: Remote

Opportunity Snapshot

Required Experience: Current or recent law school enrollment, hands-on Bluebook citation experience, and law review or law journal editing experience.

Key Responsibilities: Review citation-checking rubrics, identify gaps in citation guidelines, and develop sample cite-checking tasks.

Job Summary

We are seeking detail-oriented law students and recent law graduates with law review or law journal experience to support a legal citation project. Candidates with hands-on cite-checking experience will apply their knowledge of The Bluebook to evaluate citation guidelines, identify potential inconsistencies, and create realistic citation-checking exercises.

No prior AI experience is required. Strong Bluebook knowledge, analytical thinking, and sound editorial judgment are essential for success in this role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Review existing Bluebook and pinpoint citation (pincite) grading rubrics to identify unclear, incomplete, or inconsistently applied rules.
  • Identify citation edge cases not addressed by existing guidelines and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Create sample cite-checking tasks using source materials and citations containing realistic errors, along with corrected citations and explanations of the applicable rules.
  • Develop tasks across various citation types and difficulty levels, from basic formatting errors to complex pincite and source-support issues.
  • Apply Bluebook citation rules consistently and accurately across all submissions.
  • Escalate ambiguous citation issues to project coordinators rather than making undocumented assumptions.
  • Complete assigned tasks within established deadlines while maintaining high standards of accuracy and quality.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Current law student, preferably in the second or third year (2L or 3L), or a recent Juris Doctor (JD) graduate.
  • Prior law review or law journal experience, particularly in cite-checking or source collection.
  • Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, citation signals, and parentheticals.
  • Ability to identify citation errors, provide accurate corrections, and explain the reasoning behind each correction.
  • Excellent attention to detail and consistency when reviewing extensive legal materials.
  • Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and meet deadlines without close supervision.
  • Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is an advantage.

Selection Process

  1. Application: Submit your application and complete the screening questions.
  2. AI Interview: Complete the interview to demonstrate your skills and expertise to the client.
  3. Profile Review: The hiring team will evaluate your profile and qualifications.
  4. Onboarding: The Talent Operations team will assist you with the onboarding process.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate has practical law review or law journal cite-checking experience, a strong command of Bluebook citation rules, and the ability to assess citations critically. They can explain citation corrections clearly, recognize ambiguous cases, and develop accurate, well-structured citation-checking exercises.

About The Role

SafeRide Health is hiring a Compliance Reporting Analyst to deliver accurate, on-time reporting to our MCO clients and Medicare and Medicaid programs, with a focus on supporting the team's goal of automating more manual reporting processes. As our business grows, so does the volume of that work. Reporting directly to our Senior Reporting and Encounters Program Manager, this role will own report production, quality assurance, and submission tracking. Collaborating across all SafeRide teams, this role will have particularly strong partnerships with our Data Analytics team, as well as with Product and Operations.

This role will help shape how our reporting compliance function runs, identifying gaps, strengthening processes, and adding to building the foundation of the function to support scale as we grow. This is an exciting opportunity to make a real impact by supporting today's manual reporting, helping drive towards more automation, so members can reliably get the care they need.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • First 30 days: Absorb & Assist
    • Learn SafeRide Health's data sources, validation requirements, and submission workflows by shadowing a full reporting cycle, including the peak 1st–15th of the month.
    • Build foundational knowledge of the CFR, MCO agreements, and state Medicaid handbooks behind assigned reports.
    • Begin executing assigned reports under guidance, demonstrating accuracy in data entry, QA, and formatting.
    • Build relationships with core partners and bring a fresh lens to current manual processes, flagging gaps along the way.
  • By day 60: Contribute & Collaborate
    • Take ownership of assigned recurring reports, delivering accurate, on-time submissions.
    • Serve as the bridge between reporting needs and Data Analytics capacity, turning requests and defects into clear, actionable tickets.
    • Begin strengthening existing processes by documenting workflows and identifying inefficiencies
  • By day 90: Own & Optimize
    • Own assigned recurring government and client reporting end-to-end, setting priorities and timelines across owned reports.
    • Lead process optimization and automation efforts for client reporting in partnership with Data Analytics.
  • First 6 Months Expected Outcomes:
    • Deliver owned reports accurately and on time.
    • Serve as a foundational contributor in standing up, strengthening, and stabilizing reporting processes, including automation where it makes sense.
    • Own process improvements that strengthen SafeRide Health's compliance.
    • Serve as a foundational contributor in establishing our new reporting processes across the program, strengthening and stabilizing them so they’re repeatable and ready for automation where appropriate.
    • Showcase ownership of process optimization and strengthen our compliance through it.
    • Own process optimization efforts that strengthen SafeRide Health’s compliance and mitigate reporting risk as we scale.
  • Additional Responsibilities:
    • Perform prescribed QA checks, identifying discrepancies, broken formulas, and unexplained variances, then escalating risks before they become deadline threats.
    • Maintain current SOPs, field mappings, regulatory research, and decision logs; support repeatable, audit-ready processes.

What You’ll Bring

  • Required:
    • 2+ years of experience as a Reporting Analyst, Data Analyst, Business Analyst, or similar role working hands-on with data, including building reports, analyzing datasets, and validating data accuracy.
    • Of those 2+ years in a hands-on data role, 1+ year in the healthcare, healthcare regulatory research, and/or health plan ops space, working on regulatory analysis and preparing regulatory reports.
    • Intermediate-to-advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, data validation, and data concatenation, with strong data entry accuracy and prescribed QA discipline.
    • Working knowledge of SQL, data-query languages, or Python scripting with the ability to bridge communication with the data analytics team and understand technical data flows.
    • Familiarity with data visualization tools such as Amazon QuickSight, Tableau, or Power BI.
    • Strategic critical thinker and problem solver with the ability to use independent judgment to find answers, apply regulatory requirements to operational limitations, and understand system-wide impact.
    • Ability to manage multiple deadlines while documenting steps and gaps and keeping compliance reports and submission records audit-ready.
    • An ownership mindset and drive to grow beyond data entry into process improvement, automation, and strategic work that helps the company scale.
    • Open to travel 2-4 times per year for company or team offsites.
    • Legally authorized to work in the US.
  • Highly Preferred:
    • Medicare/Medicaid reporting experience, including navigating the CFR, MCO agreements, and state Medicaid handbooks.
    • Understanding of health plan operations, such as claims processing, utilization management, prior authorizations, and call center operations.
    • Strong project and stakeholder management skills, building trusted relationships that influence collaboratively across teams.
    • Familiarity with project management tools such as Asana, Jira, or similar collaboration platforms.

The salary range may cover multiple levels.
