jobs.excerpt: About the teamAt Zillow Group, our mission is to help more people get home.
jobs.description:
About the team

At Zillow Group, our mission is to help more people get home. The CoreTech Org delivers on this mission by building the foundational platforms, data, and developer capabilities that power every consumer, partner, and employee experience at Zillow.

You will work most closely with the Connections Platform (CP) — the engine that turns consumer interest into a connection with the right partner, owning the conversational experience, the lead funnel and follow-up workflows, and the shared agent services that sit underneath both. Increasingly, that experience is powered by LLM-based and agentic systems: agents that qualify leads, summarize and extract intelligence from conversations for partner teams, and drive proactive outreach. Beyond CP, you will be a measurement partner for the broader CoreTech Org — the foundational platforms every consumer, partner, and employee experience at Zillow is built on — wherever a hard data science problem needs an owner.

These are platforms with hundreds of touchpoints and dozens of dependent teams — and they have historically been among the hardest places at Zillow to measure well. CP itself is mid-transformation, shifting from NLP to LLM and agent-based systems, with agents increasingly built and relied on in production but no rigorous way to evaluate them yet. That combination — high dependency, hard-to-measure, and changing fast — is exactly where rigorous measurement creates the most leverage.

About the role

We are seeking a Principal Data Scientist to be a measurement and impact partner in CoreTech. This is a senior individual-contributor role embedded with the Data & Infrastructure Platform team and who will partner tightly with Product leadership.


You will own four outcomes: (1) make the impact of platform work legible — quantifying what shipped, what moved, and what didn’t, in terms leaders can act on; (2) define the metrics that matter for CP and the other platforms you take on — what belongs on a progress dashboard, what is a leading vs. lagging indicator, and what is vanity; (3) build the evaluation layer CP is missing — standing up rigorous, repeatable evals for its LLM and agentic systems (including LLM-as-a-judge) so the team can tell whether an agent actually works, not just that it shipped; and (4) operationalize and instrument those metrics and evals in partnership with engineering — getting the events emitted, the pipelines stable, the dashboards live, and the data trusted.


The defining challenge of this role is twofold. The first is measuring causal impact: CP has live, expensive, executive-facing questions that hinge on making a credible impact claim when a clean A/B test isn’t available — conversational and agent-driven flows that span a lead’s journey across sessions and channels, and changes that roll out to everyone at once. The second is establishing anevaluation feedback loop: much of CP now runs on LLM-based and agentic systems that were built by engineers with no rigorous way to measure whether they actually work. You will own how we evaluate these systems — defining the signals that matter, standing up eval and experimentation frameworks (including LLM-as-a-judge), and separating activity and adoption from genuine quality and outcomes. The same question recurs across CoreTech in many different areas, and you will need to help prove whether new features or infrastructure actually pay off, rather than trusting activity or adoption as proof. Owning these questions is the heart of the job.


This is a high-leverage, cross-Zillow role: your work will set the measurement bar for platforms every product team at Zillow depends on, and your point of view will directly shape how Data & Infrastructure Platform OKRs are written and reviewed at the executive level.

You will:

  • Define and operationalize the measurement strategy for the Connections Platform and the broader Data & Infrastructure Platform team — owning the throughline from raw events to executive dashboards and causal inference attribution.
  • Own the evaluation of CP’s LLM-based and agentic systems: design the evals, define the quality signals, and build the frameworks (including LLM-as-a-judge and using tooling such as Braintrust) that tell us whether an agent is actually working.
  • Own the causal inference and experimentation program for these teams: design and analyze A/B tests where you can, and where you can’t, build the quasi-experimental causal inference design (switchbacks, difference-in-difference, synthetic control, interrupted time-series) that produces a defensible estimate of impact. Know which method the situation calls for, what assumptions it rests on, and make the call for the best method to answer each hard question.
  • Be the credible authority on “what to measure” and “what to experiment on” for these teams — pushing back on vanity metrics, identifying the leading indicators we’ve been missing, and knowing which signals actually reflect the customer experience.
  • Own the impact dimension that platform measurement usually lacks — connecting adoption of CP’s agents and other platform investments to business and revenue outcomes, not just activity, speed, and quality signals.
  • Partner with engineering ICs to instrument the metrics: events, schemas, and pipelines needed to get quality measurements. Engineers will wire up the engine; you make the data infrastructure for these surfaces something teams can trust, and you shape what gets emitted in the first place.
  • Translate complex measurement realities into clear narratives for VP and C-level partners, including the trade-offs they need to consider.
  • Set the bar for how data science is practiced inside platform teams at Zillow , treating the platform itself as a product whose adoption, quality, and impact get measured as rigorously as any consumer product (Platform-as-a-Product measurement).
  • Help decipher the impact of product changes that are multi-dimensional at once – touching consumers, partners, and developers, and carrying real business and revenue stakes.
This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $182,100.00 - $290,900.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $173,000.00 - $276,400.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

  • Senior data scientist with internal-customer and/or platform measurement experience. 10+ years in Data Science, UX Research, or Applied Science, including meaningful time measuring products where the customer is a developer, an internal team, or a platform. You have led the measurement of platform products — where adoption, partner teams, and downstream outcomes all matter — and you know why that’s harder, not easier.
  • Fluent in evaluating complex user-facing systems. You have designed evals for products where quality is hard to pin down – using the right tool for the job, from labeled test sets and human review to LLM-as-a-judge. You can separate adoption and activity from genuine quality, turning “the experience feels better” into a defensible number.
  • Causal-inference and experimentation-fluent. You have owned the design and analysis of A/B tests and causal inference methodology in production — and you’ve expertly made the call between which method is the most appropriate to answer a hard question.
  • Metric architect, not dashboard operator. You have deep experience designing primary metrics, KPIs, OKR metric definitions, and leading and lagging indicator systems from scratch. You can tell the difference between a measurement problem and an instrumentation problem, and you fix the right one first.
  • Engineering-credible operator. You can sit with a staff engineer and design the event taxonomy, debug the methodology, and push back on the schema — not hand a spec over the wall. You write your own Python and SQL, and you’ve shipped instrumentation others can build on – repeatable, reliable, and documented enough that another team could adopt it – not just consumed what someone else produced.
  • Executive translator. You can land a measurement narrative with a VP or Senior Director without losing rigor — and you know which assumptions to surface up and which to keep in the appendix.
  • Builder-mentality individual contributor. You write your own code, model your own data, and prototype your own evals and dashboards. You raise the bar that the team’s daily work is rigorous and repeatable, and you make the ICs around you better by doing it visibly.

Preferred qualifications:

PhD and 4+ years, MS and 6+ years, or BS and 8+ years of experience in Statistics, Econometrics, Data Science, User Experience Research, Machine Learning, Operations Research, or a related quantitative field.

  • Direct experience measuring complex, production user-facing systems – for example, non-deterministic ones such as conversational, LLM-based, or agentic products (chat and voice assistants, lead or conversation funnels, agent-driven workflows).
  • Fluency with modern evaluation methods and the judgment to know which signals to trust – approaches like LLM-as-a-judge and offline/online eval harnesses, or adjacent evaluation experience.
  • Experience measuring the impact of AI or agentic tooling on real outcomes — separating adoption and activity from genuine productivity or quality gain, and reasoning about ROI against spend.
  • Experience operating inside a Platform-as-a-Product model with internal teams as customers.
  • Fluency with quasi-experimental and causal inference methods for when randomization isn’t possible — difference-in-difference, synthetic control, interrupted time-series, and switchback or interleaved designs — including the discipline to state assumptions explicitly and be clear about what you can and cannot measure.

Get to know us

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.


How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.


Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.


No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

32–36 uur | Meerdere locaties | € 3.592,96 tot € 6.171,02 bruto per maand

Wil jij niet alleen leidinggeven, maar ook écht bouwen aan de toekomst van de zorg? Als Teammanager bij Silverein krijg je de ruimte om jouw team te ontwikkelen, je eigen talenten in te zetten én vanuit jouw expertise bij te dragen aan de ontwikkeling van jouw regio.

Wat ga je doen als Teammanager?

Als Teammanager geef je leiding aan een team van 40tot 50 medewerkers op fulltime basis. Je creëert een omgeving waarin medewerkers zich kunnen ontwikkelen, verantwoordelijkheid nemen en hun talenten optimaal kunnen inzetten. Je begrijpt dat ieder team iets anders nodig heeft. Daarom pas je jouw leiderschapsstijl aan op de situatie: coachend waar het kan en sturend waar nodig. Je weet mensen met elkaar te verbinden en krijgt de ruimte om samen met jouw team verder te bouwen.

En dat bouwen nemen we letterlijk. We zoeken Teammanagers die een uitdaging niet uit de weg gaan en die energie krijgen van ontwikkelen en verbeteren. Je denkt in kansen, laat je niet snel van je koers afbrengen en ziet een lastige situatie vooral als een kans om samen verder te komen. Je kijkt naar wat er al goed gaat én ziet waar ruimte ligt om de volgende stap te zetten.

Naast de ontwikkeling van jouw team ben je verantwoordelijk voor een gezonde bedrijfsvoering. Je hebt daarbij aandacht voor onder andere formatie, budgetten, verzuim, re-integratie en het werven en behouden van medewerkers.

Ruimte voor jouw talent

Bij Silverein kijken we niet alleen naar wat de functie van jou vraagt, maar juist ook naar wat jij meebrengt. Daarom krijg je onder andere een zelfevaluatiescan waarmee we samen kijken waar jouw kracht ligt, waar jouw ontwikkelpotentieel zit en hoe je dit in de praktijk kunt inzetten.

Ook binnen jouw regio krijg je de mogelijkheid om een eigen expertise in te zetten. Weet jij bijvoorbeeld veel van het verbeteren van kwaliteit van zorg? jobs.excerpt: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale.
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity and we would be interested in applications from Germany, UK, Ireland and Spain.

The Opportunity:

Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, and traces with Grafana. It allows our customers to leverage the best open source observability software – including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, and Tempo – without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack

The Observability department is focused on enabling developers to understand the health and performance of their applications and infrastructure in any environment by providing tools to instrument their code, ingest observability data into Grafana Cloud and visualize and explore it.

The OpenTelemetry SDKs team's mission is to make sure our users succeed in instrumenting their software with OpenTelemetry. We work closely with the OpenTelemetry SIGs to make OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation libraries a success. Members of this team are experts in at least one programming language and have a broad knowledge of various other programming languages.

In this role, you will focus on a language-specific implementation of OpenTelemetry in Python, with an emphasis on OpenTelemetry for Generative AI. You will get to work in an upstream-first approach, helping accelerate the OpenTelemetry project while bringing the innovations to Grafana labs products and offerings.

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. We are looking for Engineers that are passionate about communicating with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! Engineers at Grafana also have the opportunity to contribute to Open Source communities.

At Grafana Labs, ICs have a dedicated career path and do not have to become managers to progress in their career. Staff Software Engineers at Grafana have a large amount of experience across multiple areas. They are able to estimate, plan, coordinate and deliver large tasks spanning multiple systems. They actively coach and mentor other team members in their team and are able to identify and resolve issues with technology and product processes.

What You’ll Be Doing:

You will bring your software engineering expertise to develop improvements to the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, with a strong focus on AI applications and agent workflows. This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI.

  • Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions.
  • Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality.
  • Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability.
  • Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community.
  • Support the technical direction and vision of the team, and contribute to business conversations on the OpenTelemetry strategy at Grafana Labs. Own projects from an ambiguous problem through design, implementation, testing, documentation, and release.
  • Partner in an open and respectful way. Lend your knowledge and skills to our GTM, Product and Support teams. Join customer conversations, investigate instrumentation issues, and turn what you learn into fixes and practical guidance.

As we are remote-first and our engineering organization is largely remote, we provide guidance and meet regularly using video calls, so high agency and good communication skills are a must.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

At Grafana Labs, Staff Engineers are defined by the impact they have and the people they enable. You take ownership of complex problems, set technical direction, and help others deliver improvements that matter to customers and the OpenTelemetry community.

  • 8+ years of experience in software development, with strong proficiency in Python and experience debugging production software, language internals, libraries, and asynchronous code.
  • An interest in AI applications and agent systems, and curiosity about how to instrument and troubleshoot them. Prior experience building AI systems is helpful, but not required.
  • Experience working in open-source communities. You are eager to become an active member of the OpenTelemetry community, collaborate with maintainers and users, and keep learning across languages, frameworks, and the wider observability ecosystem.
  • Familiarity with observability tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry, alongside experience with cloud-based software or systems engineering. You understand production environments and can assess operational risks.

Bonus Points For:

  • You have experience working on open source observability projects, ideally in OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.
  • Experience in Python instrumentation techniques, profiling, runtime diagnostics, or asynchronous context propagation
  • Experience in a hands-on technical leadership role, setting technical direction and leading project teams
  • Experience instrumenting AI frameworks or agent workflows, or working with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI
  • Experience contributing to or maintaining Open Source projects, with evidence of successful pull requests and community collaboration
  • Rust experience is a plus for exploring potential Python SDK performance improvements, including Rust-backed implementations.

Compensation & Rewards:

In Ireland, the compensation range for this role is EUR 121,000 - EUR 151,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Exposure & Vulnerability Management
jobs.excerpt: Your work will change lives.  Including your own.
jobs.description:
Your work will change lives. Including your own.

The Impact You’ll Make

Help shift Recursion from periodic scans to continuous, risk-driven exposure management. You’ll build multi-agent systems that take vulnerabilities from discovery to verified closure, with approval gates, audit trails, and rollback built in. You’ll replace static CVSS scores with prioritization based on reachability, attack paths, business criticality, and live exploit intelligence, so engineering teams can focus on what’s actually exploitable. By integrating remediation into ticketing and CI/CD and partnering with Engineering and IT to make secure-by-default the norm, you’ll shrink our attack surface and speed up fixes where risk is highest, helping Recursion keep decoding biology with confidence.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and deploy multi-agent systems that take an exposure from discovery to closure: analyzing it from the outside in, mapping dependencies from the inside out, generating the patch or Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) update, and validating the result. Build in approval gates, audit trails, and rollback so every automated change gets the level of review its risk calls for.
  • Move prioritization beyond static CVSS scores by building engines that rank exposures on real-time reachability, attack-path context, business criticality, and live exploit intelligence.
  • Cut through alert noise with automated verification that separates theoretical flaws from actively exploitable conditions, so engineering and DevOps teams can focus on the issues that matter.
  • Drive our Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) strategy, shifting the organization from periodic scans to a proactive, around-the-clock security posture across products, platforms, cloud and on-premise infrastructure, and corporate applications.
  • Assess the current state of our exposure and vulnerability management program and revamp the strategy to accelerate key business outcomes and support our broader zero-trust security approach.
  • Architect cloud-native discovery, asset-inventory, and remediation workflows, and integrate them with ticketing, CI/CD, and configuration management so fixes reach owners and ship without manual hand-offs.
  • Partner with Engineering and IT to embed secure-by-default practices into how products and applications are built, deployed, and patched, with remediation timelines matched to real risk.
  • Define KPIs, KCIs, and KRIs (for example mean time to remediate, exploitable-exposure backlog, and coverage of critical assets) that show how well controls are working and guide continuous improvement.
  • Support regulatory compliance by working with partner teams to design exposure and vulnerability controls that meet standards such as SOC2.

The Team You’ll Join

You will join a growing Information Security team at Recursion, focused on enabling Recursion to decode biology by providing world class secure technology services that are designed and fit for purpose. You'll collaborate with your teammates and across departments to ensure that IAM systems support the organization's broader business objectives while maintaining the highest standards of security.

The Experience You’ll Need

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in vulnerability management, exposure management, or related information security domains, including leading large-scale programs from strategy through execution in cloud-first and hybrid environments.
  • Deep understanding of security principles, with a track record of turning vulnerability data into prioritized, owned, and verified remediation.
  • Hands-on experience building or deploying AI/LLM-based agents or multi-agent systems for security or engineering workflows, including orchestration, tool use, and evaluation.
  • Working knowledge of approval workflows, audit logging, and rollback controls for automated remediation, and of the risks of agent-driven changes.
  • Proficiency in one or more programming languages (for example Python, Go, Java) and strong scripting skills for automation and integration.
  • Expert-level experience with leading vulnerability and exposure management platforms (for example Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, or equivalent) and with CTEM, attack surface management, and attack-path analysis tooling.
  • Strong command of risk-based prioritization: CVSS, EPSS, CISA KEV, reachability analysis, and threat intelligence feeds.
  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), container and Kubernetes security, and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation) for automated remediation.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines, SCA/SAST tooling, and software supply chain security, including SBOMs and dependency mapping.
  • Knowledge of operating systems (UNIX/Linux, macOS, Windows), networking, and database management systems.
  • Experience with risk management, ensuring solutions align with organizational risk tolerance and compliance requirements (SOC2, GxP, or similar).

Role Overview

The Packaging Manager role serves as a key bridge between regulatory packaging requirements, such as source/waste reduction and reuse, CAA’s materials strategy, and producer/industry design initiatives. This role ensures alignment and harmonization of packaging design approaches and best practices across jurisdictions, in keeping with the needs of CAA’s producer members.

The role serves as a technical subject matter expert on packaging transition feasibility, producer operational realities, and packaging functionality, translating complex technical and engineering concepts into actionable guidance for regulatory, policy, legal, and program teams.

The Packaging Design Manager will:

  • Contribute to overarching packaging design strategy.
  • Develop tools, guidance, and other beneficial resources that will help producers integrate eco-design principles into packaging solutions, in keeping with CAA’s design-driven eco-modulation strategy.
  • Prepare design-related submissions to regulators (such as comments on proposed regulations, exemption requests and other submissions that will facilitate compliance with state-level legislative and regulatory objectives)
  • Engage with producers, industry, and end markets to socialize the impacts of EPR laws on packaging and motivate change, including webinars.

The Manager will also contribute to the development and evolution of CAA’s design-driven eco-modulation strategy and support CAA’s broader materials strategies related to reduction, reuse, recyclability, and compost-ability; and in this regard may engage with producers, converters, reclaimers, and other interested parties directly to understand system needs and inform design solutions.

This role sits on the Circularity & Packaging Design team within the national Program Planning and Operations department, which also includes Data & Analytics, Compliance & Regulatory Affairs, Emerging States, End Markets, and Collection & Processing.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop tools, guidance and other beneficial resources that translate regulatory and materials management objectives into practical packaging design actions, and that support regulatory compliance, circular economy objectives, and alignment across multiple EPR jurisdictions.
  • Prepare regulatory submissions on technical matters (such as comments on regulatory/legislative proposals, applications for exemptions, and appeals for rule or regulatory changes to existing programs).
  • Provide technical input into state-level program plans.
  • Monitor and evaluate evolving packaging design standards from a producer perspective, identifying trends, innovations, and best practices to inform program strategy and producer guidance.
  • Support the development and implementation of holistic material reduction, reuse, recycling, and composting material strategies.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure packaging design considerations are integrated into broader materials management, recycling, and stewardship strategies, including strong end market and demand solutions.
  • Contribute to the creation, review, and continuous improvement of eco-design tools including but not limited to eco-modulated bonus and malus incentive mechanisms.
  • Engage packaging designers, producers, and other industry interest holders to promote adoption of eco-design best practices and understand and respond to evolving eco-design expectations and requirements.
  • Other job-related duties as assigned.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong understanding of the role of packaging design in driving environmental outcomes and enabling efficient and productive recycling systems (collection, sorting, reclamation and conversion).
  • Strong understanding of producer performance requirements for product packaging including product protection and use, shelf life, branding, marketing and merchandising.
  • Experience developing and implementing packaging sustainability solutions including initiatives focused on recyclability, source reduction, reuse, material transitions, and circular economy outcomes.
  • Ability to engage and collaborate with cross-functional teams and external stakeholders, including packaging designers, producers, and recyclers to advance adoption of eco-design best practices.
  • Robust knowledge of packaging materials, covered material categories, and chemicals of concern.
  • Understanding of recycling systems and end-market considerations with the ability to translate technical requirements into practical design guidance.
  • Familiarity with industry eco-design standards (e.g., reusability/recyclability/compost-ability standards) and emerging sustainability trends.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate design tradeoffs across environmental, operational, regulatory, and market considerations.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to develop, review, and maintain technically accurate guidance and program materials.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in sustainable packaging, material design and engineering, material strategy, or circular economy roles.

Compensation & Other Information

  • Location: Remote from the United States of America
  • Pay Rate: Based on a variety of factors in accordance with applicable law including the successful candidate’s relevant experience, skills, knowledge, and experience.
  • Reports To: Interim VP of Circularity & Design with future reporting to Senior Manager– Packaging Design.

    • Insurance: Articulate how GenLogs transforms motor carrier underwriting, policy compliance, chameleon carrier detection, and claims investigations.

Job Summary

Luminate Heritage is WellBe’s most technical in-house platform and supports changes across our EMR, scheduling platform and broader ecosystem. The Technical IT Project Manager is the long-term delivery owner for Heritage, accountable for turning architecture, engineering and operational dependencies into an executable roadmap. You will work credibly in code reviews, architecture sessions and SQL-based investigations; challenge scope and estimates; drive release readiness; and translate technical risk and tradeoffs into clear decisions for leadership.

  • Own delivery of the Luminate Heritage roadmap, including enhancements, technical debt, stabilization and modernization
  • Work hands-on with developers and architects to decompose technical scope, review designs, validate estimates and sequence work
  • Build and maintain a dependency map of Heritage's interfaces with Luminate 2.0, the scheduling platform and other systems, and assess the technical impact of every change
  • Coordinate release engineering: branching strategy, CI/CD readiness, environments, code freezes, deployment windows, regression scope and rollback plans
  • Investigate production issues with engineering, using logs, queries and monitoring to understand root cause and drive corrective action
  • Surface architecture, performance, scalability, security and technical-debt risks early, with impact and options

Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group - education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology - funded entirely from its own operating cash. Inflection Club is a private co-investment community for accredited investors, operators, and family offices who want direct access to pre-IPO and private-market deals in the companies shaping the future. Every deal goes through institutional-grade diligence and is executed as a Reg D 506(c) SPV. We are early, and the growth seat is the most important one we have left to fill.

Role Summary

Inflection Club is hiring a Director of Growth to build and own the engine that turns attention into qualified applications and members. This is a revenue-producing, hands-on operator role - not a campaign manager and not a generalist marketer.

You will personally find and close distribution partners (affiliates, event partners, referral channels, founder and personal-brand audiences), own the marketing infrastructure end to end, and convert founder-led LinkedIn and content attention into applications and sales. You are building from the ground up, and you take full ownership quickly.

What You Will Own

  • Growth strategy. Find new growth strategies to take the business to new heights.
  • Partner-led growth. Find, pitch, sign, and activate affiliates, event partners, referral channels, and other distribution relationships - "everywhere." You run outreach yourself; you do not wait for a list.
  • Founder and personal-brand distribution. Turn the founders' and operators' personal-brand reach (LinkedIn first) into a repeatable path from attention to application.
  • Acquisition systems. Build repeatable, measurable channels that produce qualified applications each month, and know the cost and yield of each.
  • Performance marketing. If we decide to pursue paid channels, plan, launch, and optimize performance marketing against cost per qualified application.
  • Marketing infrastructure. Own the newsletter strategy and campaigns, website and funnel, VSL and application flow, and the conversion paths from LinkedIn and other content - without relying on other team members to piece it together.
  • Conversion. Instrument the funnel from first touch to application to sale. Find the leaks, fix them, and report on them.
  • Reporting and accountability. Run a weekly growth review: pipeline, partner performance, cost per qualified application, and what is changing next.
  • Leadership. Direct contractors, agencies, and cross-functional teammates, and scale the seat into a team when the numbers justify it.

Requirements

What You Will Bring

Must have

  • A demonstrated track record of growing a comparable high-ticket membership, community, or education-style offer. Not a generalist - we want to see the numbers you moved.
  • Hands-on experience building partner-led growth: affiliates, event partners, referral channels, and distribution relationships, with named partners and results.
  • Experience driving growth through founder and personal-brand distribution, especially LinkedIn.
  • Experience owning marketing infrastructure: newsletter campaigns, website and funnel, VSL or application flow, and conversion paths.
  • Willingness to be hands-on - you will do your own partner outreach and deal-making.
  • Entrepreneurial and self-directed: you have built something from zero and do not need to be told what to do next.
  • Comfortable with data: clear on CAC, conversion rates, and payback, and able to report them plainly.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the judgment to represent a premium, compliance-aware brand.

Nice to have

  • Experience in private markets, venture, fintech, wealth, or investor-facing communities, and a network of relevant partners.
  • Existing relationships with affiliates, event organizers, or personal brands that serve accredited investors.
  • Performance marketing experience, if we decide to run paid channels.
  • Prior experience as a head or director of growth at an early-stage company.
  • Familiarity with HubSpot, ClickUp, and AI-assisted workflows.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive independent contractor compensation, with a performance component.
  • Fully remote, globally distributed team.
  • Ground-floor ownership of growth at a private co-investment club built to scale.
  • Direct exposure to institutional-grade deal flow and a high-calibre investor community.
  • Team offsites (Dubai, Costa Rica, etc).
  • Opportunity to move up based on performance and available positions.

  • Analyze and interpret vendor contracts and coverage analysis documents, providing guidance on research vs. standard of care reimbursement.

  • Advance processed vendor data, completed check request, and support to the AP team for vendor reimbursement

2025 Deloitte Technology Fast 50 Canada Recipient & Fast 500 North America Recipient 🏆
SpryPoint is modernizing how utilities serve their communities. As a high-growth software company, we're shaking up the status quo in the utility industry with the first and only truly cloud-native customer service and operations platform purpose-built for modern utilities.
Founded by industry veterans in 2011, we've grown from a profitable startup to a rapidly scaling company of 300+ employees serving 100+ utility clients across North America and the Caribbean. Our mission is simple: utility leaders should expect more from their technology providers.
Utilities face urgent demand to replace inefficient legacy systems while managing increasing operational complexity, and evolving customer expectations. With more than a decade of experience, and a track record of successful implementations spanning water, electric, and gas utilities, SpryPoint has built a reputation as a trusted and mission-critical partner to utilities across North America.
We deliver comprehensive solutions including SpryCIS, SpryEngage, SpryMobile, and SpryWallet that modernize the entire meter-to-cash process. What sets us apart? Our "updates, not upgrades" approach, user-centric design, and unwavering focus on customer success.
Backed by strategic investment from Norwest Venture Partners since 2023, and an exciting new investment partnership from Insight Partners announced in 2026, we're accelerating our growth while staying true to our core values: lead with kindness, vision with impact, radical honesty, bold disruption, keep it simple, and execute with excellence.
Join our award-winning team in transforming an essential industry that powers communities across the Americas.

Position Overview

As a Data Conversion Engineer at SpryPoint you will play a key role in supporting the transformation and migration of utility billing data from legacy systems into our modern utility and billing platform.
You will work in the Technical Services department alongside the rest of the Data Conversion team to extract, transform, and load (ETL) customer data, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, reliability, and quality. You will have opportunities to collaborate with pair programming, learn best practices in data migration, and contribute to process improvements.
This role is a great opportunity for someone early in their data engineering career who wants to build strong foundations in data transformation, conversion auditing, and process optimization within a collaborative and iterative environment.

Responsibilities

  • Lead and manage ETL migration processes across multiple concurrent projects, ensuring robust data pipeline development and timely project delivery.
  • Develop and maintain efficient extraction, transformation, and loading scripts, utilizing Python, SQL, and related data engineering tools to ensure high-quality data migrations.
  • Implement feedback-driven improvements from clients and internal teams, enhancing data conversion quality, performance, and reliability.
  • Actively contribute to data quality assurance processes and review datasets for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Conduct in-depth analysis and profiling of diverse source database schemas (including relational and non-relational legacy systems) to accurately map and facilitate successful data extraction and migration.
  • Collaborate closely with the broader Client Experience team to seamlessly integrate client data into SpryPoint products, enabling smooth and timely go-live processes.
  • Work with the Data Conversion team to establish and promote best practices, create documentation, and drive continuous improvement in data migration processes, automation, and observability.
  • Actively participate in daily standups and weekly review sessions, clearly communicating progress, raising blockers, and incorporating feedback to continuously improve data engineering tasks and processes.

Qualifications and Competencies

  • Development experience with Python and the pandas module.
  • Development experience with SQL and relational databases.
  • Experience in data migration, ETL processes, process scripting, and automation.
  • Understanding of system design and analysis.
  • A creative approach to problem-solving and learning, and an enjoyment of solving puzzles.

Our Hiring Process!

We know that looking for a new role can be both exciting and time-consuming, and we truly appreciate your effort. Here’s a peek into our hiring process for this position, so you know exactly what to expect:
 👋 Stage 1: 30-minutes Recruiter Interview
We'll dive into your professional background and experience, share more about SpryPoint and the role, and answer any burning questions you might have.
 🧑‍💻 Stage 2: Take Home Assignment
You'll have 2-3 days to complete the assignment, which focuses mainly on Python and Pandas. We’re not expecting perfection, what matters most is how you approach problem-solving!
 👥 Stage 3: 1-hour Final Technical Interview
This is a great chance to dive into your career goals, technical experience, and how we can support your growth. You’ll walk the team through your assignment, we’re just as interested in your final solution as we are in your thought process. jobs.excerpt: About the Job:LaunchDarkly is seeking a Pricing & Packaging Field Insights Lead to bring a practical, field-informed perspective to important pricing and packaging decisions.
jobs.description:
About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is seeking a Pricing & Packaging Field Insights Lead to bring a practical, field-informed perspective to important pricing and packaging decisions. This role will work across Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Deal Management, Finance, Product, and Marketing to understand how customers and field teams experience our current commercial model—and turn those insights into clear, evidence-based recommendations.

The role is designed for a commercially minded operator who can engage directly with customer-facing teams, identify recurring friction and opportunity, evaluate options, and communicate a point of view to decision-makers. The successful candidate will help ensure that pricing and packaging decisions are not only analytically sound, but also understandable, sellable, and workable in real customer conversations.

This is a role with a focused mandate: gather and synthesize field insights, assess pricing and packaging alternatives, and recommend decisions that improve clarity, customer value communication, and field execution.

Project scope and working model

  • The role will have a defined project plan, regular stakeholder reviews, and agreed decision milestones.
  • The scope may evolve as field research surfaces new evidence, but the primary outcomes will remain field insight synthesis and pricing and packaging recommendations.
  • The role is an individual-contributor position and does not include direct people management.

Responsibilities:

  • Gather and synthesize field insights
    • Design and lead the organization's structured approach to field research; interviews, listening sessions, deal review, establishing the methodology other teams adopt for surfacing pricing and packaging signal from the field.
    • Serve as the principal authority for distinguishing isolated anecdotes from repeatable, structural signal across account executives, sales leadership, solutions engineering, customer success, and deal desk; codify this judgment into frameworks others can apply.
    • Translate field feedback into strategic themes and hypotheses that shape long-term pricing and packaging direction, not just near-term decision inputs.
    • Set the standard for how field perspective is represented in pricing and packaging discussions, including the judgment calls on confidentiality and representativeness that less experienced contributors would escalate.
  • Evaluate options and recommend decisions
    • Exercise wide latitude in determining which pricing and packaging questions merit investigation, and in defining the approach, objectives and methods are largely self-determined, with accountability for outcomes that affect the function or company as a whole.
    • Serve as principal advisor and internal expert on the interaction between pricing/packaging models and field commercial behavior; erroneous judgment here carries company-wide, long-term consequences.
    • Develop decision materials that function as the authoritative reference for the problem space; evidence, options, tradeoffs, and risk, used directly by executive and senior leadership to commit to strategy.
    • Partner with Finance, Product, Revenue Operations, Deal Management, and executive leadership as a peer contributor to strategy, not just a validator of others' assumptions; shape how those functions think about pricing risk going forward.
    • Identify systemic risks: unintended incentives, inconsistent application, structural complexity before they surface in the field, and influence policy and future model design to prevent them proactively.
    • Determine when a pilot, test, or feedback loop is warranted as a matter of judgment and precedent-setting practice, not a recommendation escalated for approval.
  • Support decision readiness
    • Own the translation of approved decisions into field-wide implications, setting the narrative and framing that customer-facing teams and enablement functions build from.
    • Identify systemic gaps in guidance, tooling, training, or process; at the level of the operating model, not a single rollout that could limit adoption at scale.
    • Establish and maintain the organization's structured system of record for field evidence, decisions, and open questions, serving as the field-wide reference of record beyond any single engagement.
    • Deliver a final readout that functions as a durable, field-wide reference; findings, recommendations, decisions, and a forward-looking view of pricing and packaging strategy used to inform strategy well beyond the immediate engagement.
  • How success will be measured
    • Field research produces a clear, representative view of recurring pricing and packaging friction and opportunity.
    • Decision-makers have concise, evidence-based recommendations with transparent tradeoffs.
    • Recommendations reflect both customer value and the realities of field execution.
    • Key pricing and packaging decisions are easier for customer-facing teams to understand and apply.
    • The project leaves behind reusable insights, decision documentation, and practical next steps for ongoing ownership.

Qualifications:

  • Experience in pricing and packaging, commercial strategy, revenue operations, sales strategy, deal desk, solutions engineering, customer success, or a closely related B2B SaaS function.
  • Direct experience working with customer-facing teams and interpreting feedback from live customer or deal contexts.
  • Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, synthesize qualitative and quantitative inputs, and form a clear recommendation.
  • Strong commercial judgment, including the ability to assess customer value, field behavior, business impact, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present a point of view to both executive stakeholders and field practitioners.
  • Ability to operate independently in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment and deliver against a defined project mandate within 3–6 months.
  • Sound judgment when handling confidential customer, deal, pricing, and employee information.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level 6:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $191,800 - $263,670**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $172,600 - $237,270**
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $163,000 - $224,070**

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

About The Role

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to build and own the Product Marketing function at GenLogs. This person will help define how we talk about our products, differentiate ourselves in the market, and communicate the value of what we're building as the company grows.

Working closely with Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, you'll turn complex technical capabilities into clear messaging that resonates with our Shipper, Insurance, Public Sector, Trucking Carrier, and Broker audiences. You'll help shape the broader GenLogs story as our product portfolio evolves, while ensuring our individual products have clear positioning and value propositions.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys setting direction and building from the ground up. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we position our products, bring new capabilities to market, and establish the processes that support Product Marketing as GenLogs grows.

What You'll Do

Product Positioning & Messaging

  • Develop and evolve GenLogs’ product and platform narrative, including how we position our offerings, differentiate ourselves in the market, and communicate our value across different customer segments.
  • Translate complex technical capabilities, product strategy, and customer needs into clear explanations of what our products do, who they serve, and why they matter.

Go-to-Market Strategy & Product Launches

jobs.description:
The Proportional Representation Hub

American democracy is at a breaking point. Fewer than one in ten House races is competitive, and 97% of incumbents cruise to reelection. For most voters, the outcome is settled before a single ballot is cast. Public trust in democratic institutions keeps eroding as more voters tune out.

The problem isn't the politicians. It's the rules. U.S. elections are distorted by single-winner, winner-take-all districts. A party can win 45% of the vote across a state and still win no power. The Supreme Court's evisceration of the Voting Rights Act has made things worse, carving up communities of color and setting off a redistricting death spiral.

There is a fix, and most of the world already uses it: proportional representation. Districts elect several members, and a party that wins a third of the votes wins about a third of the seats. It ends partisan gerrymandering, reduces the polarization that fuels authoritarianism, creates more opportunity for fair representation of women and people of color, fosters more robust political parties including new, smaller parties, and makes every district competitive.

The Proportional Representation Hub has raised more than $80 million to advance proportional representation at the local, state, and federal levels. We are building a cross-partisan movement big enough to win, and a team of exceptional leaders to reshape the architecture of American democracy itself.

Position summary

The Director of State and Local Campaigns will play a pivotal role in turning the PR Hub’s state and local strategy into winning campaigns on the ground. Reporting to the Vice President of State and Local Campaigns, the Director will run day-to-day execution across a portfolio of ballot measure campaigns at the state and local level and may participate in setting strategy on legislative campaigns.

The Director will manage campaign plans, timelines, and budgets in priority geographies. They will work hand in hand with local organizers, coalition partners, consultants, and elected officials to move campaigns from early opportunity to victory.

The successful candidate has previously run a statewide electoral campaign, ballot initiative, or competitive congressional campaign. They are able to think strategically while also getting their hands dirty with the details of execution. They are highly organized, take initiative without waiting to be asked, and know how to keep multiple fast-moving campaigns on track at once.

This is a role for a proven campaign operator who is eager to help build one of the most important democracy reform efforts of the next decade.

What You’ll Do

Run Winning Campaigns

  • Lead day-to-day execution of state and local legislative and ballot measure campaigns in priority geographies.
  • Translate high-level strategy into detailed campaign plans with clear goals, timelines, budgets, and metrics to advance proportional representation and related democracy reforms.

  • Support the VP in identifying emerging state and local opportunities.

Who You Are

You are exceptionally organized and can juggle many moving pieces. You have built and managed systems that keep a team on track and are able to serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership.

Luxury Presence is building the AI growth platform for real estate. Role Overview

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to own a core part of how our clients market themselves: the websites, content, and campaigns that get them found, keep them top of mind, and turn attention into business. Our clients are real estate professionals, many of them top producers in luxury markets, and they count on us for the marketing they don't have time to do themselves.

Generating marketing content is easy now. Generating content a top agent is proud to put their name on is not. That bar, across every channel our clients use, is the game we're in. So is proving what works: showing clients how their channels feed each other and which ones are actually driving business.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role with close collaboration across engineering, design, AI/ML, client success, and sales. You'll own a product area end to end, set its strategy, and grow its scope as we expand into new channels.

What You'll Do

  • Own the product strategy, roadmap, and results for a set of AI-powered marketing products, starting with how our clients get discovered and the content we create for them
  • Make sure our clients get found, whether a prospective buyer or seller searches on Google or asks an AI assistant who to call
  • Raise the quality bar on everything we create on our clients' behalf, so it sounds like them and reflects the brand they've built
  • Design how channels work together, so a client's website, content, email, and social reinforce each other instead of running as separate tools
  • Build the measurement and attribution that show clients, and us, how those channels drive each other and which ones are actually producing business
  • Run structured betas with real clients, set clear hypotheses up front, and keep iterating until clients would be upset to lose what you've built
  • Build the business case for your roadmap and tie it to adoption, retention, and revenue
  • Ship with your own engineering and design partners, and work closely with client success and sales so launches land

Who You Are

  • 7+ years of product management, including owning a product line end to end where you were accountable for adoption, outcomes, and revenue
  • Marketing taste. You can tell great marketing from generic, and you know how a premium brand should and shouldn't show up. You'd catch the post that makes a client look bad before it ships
  • Multichannel instincts. You understand how search, content, email, social, and paid work together as a system, and you want to see the numbers move across all of them, not just one
  • Experience building marketing technology: products businesses use to grow their own customer base
  • Solid SEO fundamentals, and a view of discovery that goes beyond the website to reviews, social, and what people say about a business across the web
  • You run your area like a business. You build the case before you build the product, and you own the result
  • Close to your customers. You talk to them often and can explain why something matters in their terms
  • You create momentum in ambiguity. You narrow the problem, make a call, and move before every question is answered
  • A communicator who can get a room excited, from engineers to executives to client success, and who earns trust across teams you don't manage
  • You learn fast and use AI as a normal part of how you work: to research, to prototype, and to get to ground truth quickly

Preferred Qualifications

  • Product experience at a company serving small businesses or solo operators who judge you on results, such as Shopify, Squarespace, Mailchimp, HubSpot, Square, or Yelp
  • You've built email, lifecycle, or campaign tools, or products that generate marketing content with AI
  • Hands-on experience with marketing analytics or attribution products
  • Familiarity with premium or luxury brands and how they market differently
  • Experience at a platform where one change reaches many customers' sites or accounts at once
  • A background in content, editorial, or brand work

Join us in shaping the future of real estate

The real estate industry is in the midst of a seismic shift, and the future belongs to those who break new ground. As one of the fastest-growing companies in the proptech and marketing sectors, Luxury Presence challenges the status quo of what technology can do for real estate agents, leaders, and brokerages.
We're a team of agile and tenacious innovators working collaboratively to drive the industry forward. Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About this role:

As a Staff Product Designer at Samsara, you will set a vision and ship work that shapes the way our customers and internal teams operate. You will partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders, set the interaction patterns and visual systems other designers build on, and build direct relationships with our most strategic customers.

This is a remote role open to candidates residing in the US.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact: helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead large, ambiguous initiatives that span multiple product areas, from problem framing through launch and iteration.
  • Be a taste maker and demonstrate good judgement in your domain.
  • Regularly meet and engage with our most strategic customers to bring the customer voice alongside product data into product decisions.
  • Leverage AI tools through every step of the process, defining new ways of working and democratizing design at Samsara.
  • Stay well informed on the emerging trends, tools, and technology. Give back to the community.
  • Ship code to production across our design system, web products, and mobile apps.
  • Set the bar for what great looks like through building and shipping.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 10+ years of product design experience designing UX/UI for web and mobile applications, with a track record of leading work that spans multiple product areas.
  • A strong portfolio and/or case studies showing design craft and quantified impact at the level of multiple product areas or platform-wide systems, not just a single feature. We cannot consider applications without a portfolio at this time.
  • Deep interaction and visual design skills, with the judgment to define new patterns other designers and teams build on.
  • AI tools in your regular design practice (e.g., Cursor, Figma Make), with shipped work you can attribute to them.
  • Experience mentoring designers formally and informally.
  • Experience partnering with senior leadership.

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$143,640—$256,500 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

The Majors sales team is responsible for revenue growth in new and existing customers that represent the largest prospective accounts for Samsara by total addressable opportunity.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US and requires living in the EST timezone.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
  • Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales processes in complex sales campaigns
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role with Enterprise customers
  • Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $500k+ ARR transactions
  • Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships
  • Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience working with a line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
  • Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)
  • Passion for the world of operations!

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) for full-time employees for this position is below. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary
$350,000—$350,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co.
